electionType: Montville Township Committee, Board of Education & General Election
councilStructure: Township of Montville operates under the Township Committee form of government. 5 Committee members are elected at-large for staggered 3-year terms, annually selecting one member as Mayor. In 2026, voters elect 2 Township Committee members, alongside 3 School Board trustees.
certifiedTaxRateContext: 2.418% Total Certified Tax Rate (2026). Equalization Ratio 88.2%.
unanimousHealthBenefitPledge: Township Committee members and BOE trustees adhere strictly to state ethics guidelines, health benefit contribution statutes, and public contracting laws.

councilCandidates.name: Matthew S. Kayne
councilCandidates.experience: Longtime Montville Committeeman with extensive private sector commercial and municipal budgeting expertise.
councilCandidates.tagline: Fiscal conservatism, protecting Montville's AAA credit rating, and rigorous open space conservation.

keyPlatformPillars.title: Low Debt & Tax Cap Discipline
bullets: Maintained one of Morris County's most prudent debt-to-valuation ratios.
Consistently keeps municipal tax levy increases well beneath the statutory 2% limit.
Prioritizes pay-as-you-go capital budgeting for vehicle and equipment upgrades.

keyPlatformPillars.title: Zoning Defense & Suburban Character
bullets: Vigorously defends Montville's master plan against predatory high-density residential rezonings.
Collaborates with Morris County Open Space Trust to protect sensitive ridge lands and watersheds.
Protects neighborhood aesthetics while supporting compliant local commercial ratables.

councilCandidates.name: June B. Witty
councilCandidates.experience: Montville Township Committeewoman (term ending December 31, 2026); attorney with extensive municipal law, land use, and municipal budgeting background.
councilCandidates.tagline: Protecting neighborhood zoning, infrastructure resilience, and public safety support.

keyPlatformPillars.title: Police & Volunteer Emergency Services
bullets: Ensuring Montville Police have cutting-edge equipment, patrol vehicles, and training.
Providing capital support and modern apparatus for Montville, Pine Brook, and Towaco volunteer fire departments.
Enhancing school resource officer (SRO) coordination with Montville public schools.

keyPlatformPillars.title: Roadways & Flood Mitigation
bullets: Aggressive multi-year road resurfacing program across all three sections of Montville.
Maintaining stormwater retention ponds and clearing drainage easements before severe storms.
Upgrading water utility infrastructure without raising municipal utility tax rates.

councilCandidates.name: Emily Ryzuk
councilCandidates.tagline: Transparent municipal planning, proactive stormwater management, and pedestrian safety.

keyPlatformPillars.title: Transparency & Community Voice
bullets: Implementing interactive digital town halls and transparent online tracking of township contracts.
Broadening resident participation on planning and environmental advisory commissions.
Publishing plain-English quarterly summaries of municipal revenue and spending.

keyPlatformPillars.title: Green Infrastructure & Climate Resilience
bullets: Utilizing federal and state clean water grants to reinforce vulnerable stormwater basins.
Creating continuous pedestrian sidewalks and bike routes connecting Towaco and Pine Brook.
Promoting municipal solar initiatives to reduce town utility operating expenses.

councilCandidates.name: David Seffer
councilCandidates.tagline: Revitalizing Towaco business district, fiscal transparency, and smart infrastructure investment.

keyPlatformPillars.title: Business District Vitality & Tax Diversification
bullets: Strengthening commercial ratables in Route 46 and Towaco village centers to ease residential tax pressure.
Conducting forensic audits of municipal vendor contracts to identify competitive savings.
Pursuing interlocal shared service agreements with neighboring Morris County municipalities.

keyPlatformPillars.title: Modernizing Municipal Facilities
bullets: Refurbishing township recreational parks and youth sports fields.
Accelerating lead water service line replacements with zero cost to residential property owners.
Improving traffic flow and signal synchronization along Route 202 and Changebridge Road.
